heard: In 1972, a blinding fireball streaked across the sky, never hitting ground. On August 10, a truck-sized space rock entered the atmosphere over the state of Utah. Moving at 15 kilometers per second, the object glowed bright enough for people to film. Tourists in Wyoming watched the trail while a sonic boom shook the air. Military surveillance, satellites tracked the object, spending 100 seconds skipping like a stone. Instead of crashing, the meteoroid merely grazed the atmosphere and rebounded back into interplanetary space. Czech astronomer Zdenek Seplicha determined this brief encounter, permanently shifted the rock's entire orbit. Not a single solid fragment reached the ground because the world only watched.
